reason: The cited evidence does not directly address Mg–Al–Cu–Zn–Gd alloys or the specific claims about diffusion-driven segregation, protective oxide formation, and corrosion improvement. E1 discusses phase partitioning in a different alloy system, E2 only states an aim without results, and E3 mentions solid solutions and intermetallics in other lightweight alloys but not the proposed mechanism. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: As-cast Mg-containing lightweight HEAs form a non-equilibrium mixture of solid solution and intermetallic phases
Post-casting annealing enables diffusion-driven phase partitioning and segregation of Al and Gd
Segregation of Al and Gd forms a refined intermetallic network and compositional gradients
This evolved microstructure promotes a continuous, adherent protective oxide scale (Al2O3/MgO/Gd oxides) during high-temperature oxidation
The evolved microstructure reduces micro-galvanic coupling and improves corrosion resistance
